Maya Chen: Heads-up — customer call tomorrow about Private Deploy onprem networking; they pushed back on our 'managed egress' requirement. Need to align on acceptance criteria.
Tom B: Can you paste the specific ask? Is this the same tenant that needs BGP?
Maya Chen: Yep. 3 things: static egress IPs, ability for customer to manage their own NAT/BGP, and audit logs exported to their SIEM.
Alex Rivera: Quick note: our current PRD assumes we manage egress IPs for simplicity. Allowing customer-managed egress means we need two modes: 'redwood-managed' and 'customer-managed'.
Sara Patel: For launch gating we need: (1) e2e test hooking up to customer BGP session, (2) infra automation for onprem handshake, (3) docs + runbook.
Jon Park: Edge case: what if customer configures overlapping IPs or announces more-specific prefixes? Need reject/validation rules + clear rollback.
Tom B: +1. Also we should define SLA differences: customer-managed egress => no per-tenant IP failover guarantees. Put in PRD.
Maya Chen: Can someone draft acceptance criteria bullets? I'll own negotiations with customer.
Alex Rivera: Draft:
- Customer can supply BGP ASN and prefix list via V2 API
- System validates prefixes are non-overlapping with platform control plane
- We establish a BGP session using MD5 auth and confirm routes
- Audit logs forwarded to customer SIEM within 2 minutes
- Fallback policy: if BGP fails, traffic routes via 'managed' path for 5 mins, then circuit down

Sara Patel: Also add monitoring: route flaps >3/min triggers paging, and automated revert if risk score > 0.8
Maya Chen: This looks good. Next steps: Alex to turn into a short RFC for eng-platform + eng-oncall; Sara to outline test matrix; Tom to update pricing/launch docs.
SRE Bot: Deployment checklist created: https://go/repo/checklists/pvt-egress-1979012345
Tom B: cc @legal — we need to confirm customer indemnity for self-managed networking.
Maya Chen: Thanks all — will sync tomorrow 10am PT. :thumbsup:
